column1: # GameActionData TYPE -> its descriptor key list (#271/#485). Dumped by tools/ghidra/DumpGameActionTypes.java.
# The window 0xCF09..0xD026 is the CLIENT'S registered range, stated twice in FUN_008c3910 - the assert bounds at
# 0x11d (= 0xD026 - 0xCF09) against `i_nGameAction < e_Type_GC_GameAction_End`, and an out-of-range id is CLAMPED to
# the first entry. 286 types, nothing past them; the descriptor table has no rows to read beyond it.
# ⚠️ The ids here are ENUM ids. `gameaction_types.json` also carries a `typeId` (Hit = typeId 53005 / enumId 53002)
# and the two diverge - an id like 0xD331 is a typeId, not a type past the end of this table.
# ⭐ `widthWords` = 8 + the number of keys, on all 260 rows with NO exception - so the descriptor's own WIDTH states
# how many keys a type has, and it reads statically even where the key ARRAY does not.
# ⚠️ That RETIRES this file's old warning, which said the blank `keys` cells were blank "because the descriptor
# table is BSS, so a static read sees zeros" and "need a live dump". They do not. Every blank row reads width
# EXACTLY 8 - the header-only size - and the blank set is EXACTLY the width-8 set (57 rows). A type whose key array
# was hidden but non-empty would show width > 8 with nothing beside it, and there is not one. So those 57 carry no
# fields at all, `StartFlymode` (53138) among them - which is what makes the empty key list `.fly` sends CORRECT
# rather than an assumption (#485). Gated by GameActionKeyListTests.DescriptorWidth_IsEightPlusTheKeyCount_*.
